A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Bcl‐2, an anti‐apoptotic protein, and Fas, a pro‐apoptotic molecule, are expressed in the glomerulus of lupus patients and their serum levels are significantly higher than those of normal individuals.
Bcl‐2 is associated with mesangial cells, whereas Fas is associated with both mesangial cells and glomerular epithelial cells in lupus nephritic kidneys.
the glomerular and serum Bcl‐ 2 and Fas expression are elevated in lupus patients, and these proteins are involved in the pathogenesis of glomerular injury in lupus nephritides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the glomerulus is not a static organ but a dynamic structure that undergoes continuous turnover and renewal of its cells, a process that is controlled by the balance between pro‐survival and pro‐death signals.

the glomerular expression, serum levels and the correlation between Bcl‐2/Fas and the chronicity indices in lupus patients suggest that the glomeruli are a source of Bcl‐ 2 and Fas production and that these proteins may play a role in glomerular damage during evolution of lupes nephritis.
Bcl‐2 protein expression in the kidneys may be a marker of chronic renal injury.
